data_types.description: Arbitrary binary buffer intended to contain a STUN/TURN message as defined by RFC 5389 and related TURN specs. Begins with a 20-byte STUN header (type, length, magic cookie 0x2112A442, and 96-bit transaction ID), followed by zero or more TLV attributes, possibly padded to 32-bit boundaries. Data may be well-formed or malformed for fuzzing.

Generic NUL-terminated human-readable string encoded as UTF-8 or ASCII. May contain any Unicode code points valid in UTF-8; for ASCII, bytes 0x20–0x7E are typical but fuzzing may include wider ranges. Used where APIs expect textual fields like error reason phrases.

    0x0008,  # CreatePermission (TURN)
    0x0009,  # ChannelBind (TURN)

    'MAPPED-ADDRESS': 0x0001,
    'USERNAME': 0x0006,
    'MESSAGE-INTEGRITY': 0x0008,
    'ERROR-CODE': 0x0009,
    'UNKNOWN-ATTRIBUTES': 0x000A,
    'REALM': 0x0014,
    'NONCE': 0x0015,
    'XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS': 0x0020,
    'SOFTWARE': 0x8022,
    'ALTERNATE-SERVER': 0x8023,
    'FINGERPRINT': 0x8028,
    # TURN:
    'CHANNEL-NUMBER': 0x000C,
    'LIFETIME': 0x000D,
    'XOR-PEER-ADDRESS': 0x0012,
    'DATA': 0x0013,
    'XOR-RELAYED-ADDRESS': 0x0016,
    'REQUESTED-TRANSPORT': 0x0019,
    'DONT-FRAGMENT': 0x001A,
    'EVEN-PORT': 0x0018,
    'RESERVATION-TOKEN': 0x0022,
}

FINGERPRINT_XOR = 0x5354554E

# Utilities

def _stun_type(method: int, cls: int) -> int:
    # RFC5389 message type encoding
    # 0b00MM MMMM MMMM with class bits mixed: C1 at bit 4, C0 at bit 7
    m = method & 0x0FFF
    c0 = (cls & 1)
    c1 = (cls >> 1) & 1
    return (m & 0x0F80) << 2 | (m & 0x0070) << 1 | (m & 0x000F) | (c0 << 4) | (c1 << 8)


def _pad4(n: int) -> int:
    return (4 - (n & 3)) & 3


def _rand_tid(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rnd.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(12))


def _attr_header(attr_type: int, length: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('!HH', attr_type, length)


def _attr_string(attr_type: int, s: bytes) -> bytes:
    h = _attr_header(attr_type, len(s))
    pad = b'\x00' * _pad4(len(s))
    return h + s + pad


def _attr_u32(attr_type: int, val: int) -> bytes:
    v = struct.pack('!I', val & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    return _attr_header(attr_type, 4) + v


def _attr_u16(attr_type: int, val: int) -> bytes:
    v = struct.pack('!H', val & 0xFFFF)
    pad = b'\x00' * 2  # 2 bytes padding to 4
    return _attr_header(attr_type, 2) + v + pad


def _attr_error_code(code: int, reason: bytes) -> bytes:
    # ERROR-CODE value: 4 bytes header (Class/Number) + reason phrase
    # Class = code // 100 (3 bits), Number = code % 100 (7 bits)
    cls = (code // 100) & 0x07
    num = code % 100
    # First 2 bytes zero, then 1 byte for class bits in high 3 bits, then number
    v = struct.pack('!H', 0) + bytes([(cls << 5) & 0xE0]) + bytes([num & 0x7F]) + reason
    # length excludes padding
    pad = b'\x00' * _pad4(len(v))
    return _attr_header(ATTR['ERROR-CODE'], len(v)) + v + pad


def _encode_addr(addr_family: int, ip_bytes: bytes, port: int, xor: bool, tid: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Address attribute value: 0x00 | family (1 byte), port (2), address (4 or 16)
    if xor:
        # XOR with magic cookie and TID
        xport = (port ^ (MAGIC_COOKIE >> 16)) & 0xFFFF
        if addr_family == 0x01:  # IPv4
            xip = struct.pack('!I', struct.unpack('!I', ip_bytes)[0] ^ MAGIC_COOKIE)
        else:  # IPv6
            cookie = struct.pack('!I', MAGIC_COOKIE)
            mask = cookie + tid
            xip = bytes(a ^ b for a, b in zip(ip_bytes, mask))
    else:
        xport = port
        xip = ip_bytes
    val = bytes([0x00, addr_family & 0xFF]) + struct.pack('!H', xport) + xip
    return val


def _attr_address(rnd: random.Random, attr_type: int, xor: bool, tid: bytes) -> bytes:
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        # IPv4
        family = 0x01
        # Choose interesting IPv4s
        candidates = [
            b'\x7F\x00\x00\x01',  # 127.0.0.1
            b'\x00\x00\x00\x00',  # 0.0.0.0
            b'\xFF\xFF\xFF\xFF',  # 255.255.255.255
            b'\xC0\xA8\x01\x01',  # 192.168.1.1
            b'\x08\x08\x08\x08',  # 8.8.8.8
        ]
        ip = rnd.choice(candidates)
    else:
        # IPv6
        family = 0x02
        candidates6 = [
            bytes(16),  # ::
            b'\x00'*15 + b'\x01',  # ::1
            b'\xfe\x80' + b'\x00'*14,  # fe80::
            b'\x20\x01' + b'\x0d\xb8' + b'\x00'*12,  # 2001:db8::
        ]
        ip = rnd.choice(candidates6)
    port = rnd.randrange(1, 65535)
    val = _encode_addr(family, ip, port, xor, tid)
    pad = b'\x00' * _pad4(len(val))
    return _attr_header(attr_type, len(val)) + val + pad


def _crc32(data: bytes) -> int:
    # RFC 5389 fingerprint uses CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3) of entire message up to fingerprint attribute,
    # then XOR with 0x5354554E. Use binascii.crc32 which returns signed on some Python versions,
    # so mask to 32 bits.
    import binascii
    return binascii.crc32(data) & 0xFFFFFFFF


def _with_fingerprint(msg: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Append FINGERPRINT attribute
    crc = _crc32(msg)
    fp = (crc ^ FINGERPRINT_XOR) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    attr = _attr_u32(ATTR['FINGERPRINT'], fp)
    # Update header length (only attribute value length counts, header 4 bytes included in overall attr)
    # STUN length is size of attributes after the 20-byte header
    body = msg[20:] + attr
    hdr = msg[:2] + struct.pack('!H', len(body)) + msg[4:20]
    return hdr + body


def _build_stun_message(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    method = rnd.choice(METHODS)
    cls = rnd.choice(CLASSES)
    mtype = _stun_type(method, cls)
    tid = _rand_tid(rnd)

    attrs = []

    # Add a mixture of attributes
    # USERNAME/REALM/NONCE/ SOFTWARE strings
    def rand_ascii(nmin: int, nmax: int) -> bytes:
        ln = rnd.randrange(nmin, nmax+1)
        alphabet = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789-_/.@"
        return bytes(rnd.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(ln))

    if rnd.random() < 0.6:
        attrs.append(_attr_string(ATTR['USERNAME'], rand_ascii(1, 16)))
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        attrs.append(_attr_string(ATTR['REALM'], rand_ascii(4, 20)))
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        attrs.append(_attr_string(ATTR['NONCE'], rand_ascii(8, 24)))
    if rnd.random() < 0.4:
        attrs.append(_attr_string(ATTR['SOFTWARE'], rand_ascii(3, 24)))

    # Address attributes
    if rnd.random() < 0.7:
        attrs.append(_attr_address(rnd, ATTR['XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS'], True, tid))
    if rnd.random() < 0.3:
        attrs.append(_attr_address(rnd, ATTR['ALTERNATE-SERVER'], False, tid))

    # TURN attributes
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        # REQUESTED-TRANSPORT: first byte protocol, rest zeros
        proto = rnd.choice([17, 6])  # UDP=17, TCP=6
        val = bytes([proto, 0, 0, 0])
        attrs.append(_attr_header(ATTR['REQUESTED-TRANSPORT'], 4) + val)
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        attrs.append(_attr_u32(ATTR['LIFETIME'], rnd.randrange(30, 3600)))
    if rnd.random() < 0.3:
        # EVEN-PORT: one byte flags, pad 3
        flag = bytes([0x80 if rnd.random() < 0.5 else 0x00])
        attrs.append(_attr_header(ATTR['EVEN-PORT'], 1) + flag + b'\x00\x00\x00')
    if rnd.random() < 0.3:
        # CHANNEL-NUMBER: 0x4000-0x7FFF, with RFFU bytes
        ch = rnd.randrange(0x4000, 0x8000)
        attrs.append(_attr_header(ATTR['CHANNEL-NUMBER'], 4) + struct.pack('!H', ch) + b'\x00\x00')

    # ERROR-CODE occasionally (for error class)
    if cls == 3 and rnd.random() < 0.8:
        code = rnd.choice([400, 401, 420, 438, 500, 486])
        attrs.append(_attr_error_code(code, rand_ascii(4, 20)))

    # Optionally UNKNOWN-ATTRIBUTES with a few 16-bit codes
    if rnd.random() < 0.25:
        unknowns = [rnd.randrange(0, 0x10000) for _ in range(rnd.randrange(1, 5))]
        val = b''.join(struct.pack('!H', u & 0xFFFF) for u in unknowns)
        pad = b'\x00' * _pad4(len(val))
        attrs.append(_attr_header(ATTR['UNKNOWN-ATTRIBUTES'], len(val)) + val + pad)

    # Assemble header and body
    body = b''.join(attrs)
    hdr = struct.pack('!HHI', mtype, len(body), MAGIC_COOKIE) + tid
    msg = hdr + body

    # Optionally add FINGERPRINT (valid)
    if rnd.random() < 0.6:
        msg = _with_fingerprint(msg)

    # Ensure size cap
    if len(msg) > 4096:
        msg = msg[:4096]
    return msg


def _build_channel_data(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # TURN ChannelData: 2 bytes channel number (0x4000-0x7FFF), 2 bytes length, then data
    ch = rnd.randrange(0x4000, 0x8000)
    # Keep payload modest to stay under cap
    pay_len = rnd.randrange(0, 256)
    payload = bytes(rnd.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(pay_len))
    # Optional padding to 4-byte boundary for certain implementations
    pad = b''
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        pad = b'\x00' * _pad4(pay_len)
    return struct.pack('!HH', ch, pay_len) + payload + pad


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose between STUN message and ChannelData frame; bias towards STUN, which most stubs expect
    if rnd.random() < 0.8:
        return _build_stun_message(rnd)
    else:
        return _build_channel_data(rnd)

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# We generate valid UTF-8/ASCII NUL-terminated strings tailored to STUN/TURN/OAuth usage in stubs.
# The returned bytes will be consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR and similar to seed construction of
# - STUN reason phrases
# - usernames/realms/passwords
# - server names and algorithm identifiers
# - small attribute payloads
# Guidelines:
# - Provide multiple NUL-terminated strings concatenated, separated by '\n' to allow the fuzzing
#   harness to slice them as independent FUZZ_PARAM_STR invocations.
# - Keep content valid UTF-8; include a mix of ASCII tokens and plausible STUN/TURN/OAuth values.
# - Limit total size <= 4096 bytes.

ASCII_WORDS = [
    "OK", "Error", "Unauthorized", "Forbidden", "Not Found", "Try Again",
    "Bad Request", "Integrity Check Failed", "Missing Attribute", "Unsupported Feature",
    "nonce", "realm", "username", "password", "mobile-id", "token", "kid", "alg",
    "turn", "stun", "allocate", "channelbind", "binding", "udp", "tcp",
]

HTTP_REASONS = [
    "200 Success", "300 Try Alternate", "400 Bad Request", "401 Unauthorized",
    "420 Unknown Attribute", "438 Stale Nonce", "430 Stale Credentials",
    "431 Integrity Check Failure", "500 Server Error", "600 Global Failure"
]

SERVER_NAMES = [
    "turn.example.org", "stun.example.com", "api.service.local", "[2001:db8::1]",
    "turn-ipv4-1.local", "stun-ipv6.service", "srv.example", "auth.example.net"
]

OAUTH_ALGS = ["A256GCM", "A128GCM"]

# Generate a printable ASCII segment with optional extended UTF-8

def gen_text(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int, ascii_only: bool = True) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    if ascii_only:
        # Printable ASCII plus spaces and punctuation
        chars = []
        for _ in range(n):
            # favor alpha-num but include punctuation
            p = rng.random()
            if p < 0.6:
                c = rng.choice("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789")
            elif p < 0.8:
                c = rng.choice(" -_.:/[]@")
            else:
                c = rng.choice(",;!?#()+*")
            chars.append(c)
        return "".join(chars)
    else:
        # Mix ASCII and some valid UTF-8 sequences
        out = bytearray()
        while len(out) < n:
            p = rng.random()
            if p < 0.75:
                out.append(rng.randrange(0x20, 0x7F))
            elif p < 0.9:
                # 2-byte UTF-8
                u = rng.randrange(0x80, 0x7FF)
                out.extend(chr(u).encode('utf-8'))
            else:
                # 3-byte UTF-8 (avoid surrogates)
                u = rng.randrange(0x800, 0xD7FF)
                out.extend(chr(u).encode('utf-8'))
        try:
            return out[:n].decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
        except Exception:
            return out[:n].decode('latin1', errors='ignore')

# Build sections aimed at various consumers in the stubs

def build_reason_lines(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    lines = []
    # Include a set of canonical STUN-like reason phrases
    for s in HTTP_REASONS:
        lines.append(s)
    # Add some random readable reasons with varying length
    for _ in range(rng.randint(4, 8)):
        lines.append(gen_text(rng, 8, 48, ascii_only=False))
    return lines


def build_credentials(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    lines = []
    # Usernames
    for u in ["user", "alice", "bob", "carol", "turn-user", gen_text(rng, 4, 12)]:
        lines.append(u)
    # Realms
    for r in ["example.org", "example.com", "voip.local", gen_text(rng, 6, 18)]:
        lines.append(r)
    # Passwords (short and longer)
    for p in ["s3cret", "password", "P@55w0rd!", gen_text(rng, 6, 32)]:
        lines.append(p)
    return lines


def build_server_names(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    lines = []
    lines.extend(SERVER_NAMES)
    # Some IPv4 and IPv6 textual hosts
    for _ in range(3):
        v = rng.getrandbits(32)
        ipv4 = f"{(v>>24)&0xFF}.{(v>>16)&0xFF}.{(v>>8)&0xFF}.{v&0xFF}"
        lines.append(ipv4)
    # Simple IPv6 literals
    for _ in range(3):
        hextets = [f"{rng.getrandbits(16):x}" for _ in range(8)]
        lines.append(":".join(hextets))
        lines.append(f"[{':'.join(hextets)}]:{rng.randrange(0,65536)}")
    return lines


def build_oauth_fields(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    lines = []
    # kid, nonce, algorithm id strings
    for _ in range(4):
        lines.append(gen_text(rng, 4, 16))
    lines.extend(OAUTH_ALGS)
    # Some base64-like strings for token content
    alphabet = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/="
    for _ in range(4):
        n = rng.randint(16, 64)
        lines.append("".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n)))
    return lines


def build_misc_payloads(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    lines = []
    # Small attribute payloads and names for print_bin_func
    lines.extend(ASCII_WORDS)
    for _ in range(10):
        lines.append(gen_text(rng, 1, 32))
    return lines


def pack_sections(sections: List[List[str]], max_total: int = 4096) -> bytes:
    # Join all lines with NUL terminators to fit FUZZ_PARAM_STR expectations; also include newlines.
    # Many fuzz harnesses read byte ranges; we ensure each string is self-terminated.
    out = bytearray()
    for group in sections:
        for s in group:
            b = s.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00"  # explicit NUL termination
            if len(out) + len(b) > max_total:
                return bytes(out)
            out.extend(b)
        # Group separator to help tokenization variety
        sep = b"\n\x00"
        if len(out) + len(sep) <= max_total:
            out.extend(sep)
    return bytes(out[:max_total])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    sections: List[List[str]] = []
    sections.append(build_reason_lines(rng))
    sections.append(build_credentials(rng))
    sections.append(build_server_names(rng))
    sections.append(build_oauth_fields(rng))
    sections.append(build_misc_payloads(rng))

    payload = pack_sections(sections, max_total=4096)

    # Ensure non-empty; fallback to a simple default if needed
    if not payload:
        return b"OK\x00Error\x00stun.example.com\x00"
    return payload
